title: Completeness: Henkin witnesses and countable models
summary: Give witnesses names, decide sentences consistently, and construct a countable term model; deduce completeness of first-order deduction.
abstract: If a set of first-order axioms never leads to a contradiction, must there be a structure in which they are all true? In a countable language, we can build one directly. We add names for witnesses to existential statements, consistently decide each sentence, and use closed terms as names for the elements of a model. Terms that the theory proves equal represent the same element. The resulting model shows that every semantic consequence of the axioms has a finite formal proof, and that consistent axioms in a countable language always have a finite or countably infinite model.
